sources.entry: Vortix - Terminal UI for WireGuard and OpenVPN with multi-tunnel control, real-time telemetry, and leak guarding.

summary.one_liner: Vortix is a keyboard-driven terminal UI (with a CLI and JSON output) for managing multiple WireGuard and OpenVPN tunnels, showing live network telemetry and checking for IP, IPv6, and DNS leaks.
summary.what_it_does: Vortix imports WireGuard .conf, OpenVPN .ovpn/.conf, and NetBird .netbird profiles, and connects them from an interactive dashboard or the command line. It runs multiple tunnels at once, distinguishing the default-route tunnel from split-route tunnels, with a Switch or Cancel choice when routes conflict. It shows throughput, latency, jitter, packet loss, public IP, ISP, and location. A Security Guard panel reports IPv4/IPv6 exposure, DNS policy, encryption, and kill-switch state as one verdict. It orchestrates the system wg, wg-quick, and openvpn tools rather than implementing the protocols itself.
use_cases: Manage several WireGuard or OpenVPN profiles at once
Check whether a VPN connection leaks IPv4, IPv6, or DNS traffic
Monitor tunnel throughput, latency, and packet loss in a terminal
Connect and disconnect VPN tunnels over SSH
Script VPN control with JSON output and exit codes
Enable a firewall kill switch for a tunnel on macOS or Linux
notable: Distinguishes the default-route tunnel from split-route tunnels running side by side
Security Guard gives one verdict covering IPv4, IPv6, DNS, encryption, and kill-switch state
Kill switch modes: off, block-on-drop, and vpn-only
Versioned JSON envelope, NDJSON watch streams, and stable exit codes for automation
caveats: Requires the system wireguard-tools and openvpn packages to be installed separately unless installed via .deb or .rpm
Changing tunnels, routes, DNS, or the firewall requires root
macOS is the primary development platform; Linux is tested on Ubuntu and Fedora in CI
